title: [foreman:P2] streamUrl(fileId) is loaded by the browser itself, so file preview/download 401s in a token-only static build
detail: Residual of DF-HERMES-CANOPY-13 (8c45439). GET /api/v1/files/{id}/stream is auth-gated by the same middleware, but streamUrl(fileId) (frontend/src/lib/fileApi.ts:204) is a bare URL handed to the browser: ViewerHost.tsx:437 renders it as <a href download> and ViewerHost.tsx:297/349 inject it into the sandboxed viewer iframes (image/pdf/media viewers read boot.streamUrl). Those loads are issued by the browser, not by our fetch code, so they cannot carry Authorization - preview/download works in dev and behind a token-injecting proxy, but 401s (TOKEN_MISSING) whenever the only token is VITE_API_TOKEN/localStorage['canopy.token']. Acceptance: either fetch-to-blob + objectURL (viewer-side change, revoke the URL on unmount) or an explicitly documented 'the proxy is required for file streaming' limitation that the README states as such; prove with a test that a token-resolving build does not hand a bare streamUrl to the DOM.

title: [foreman:P3] service-worker offline queue replays a stale bearer token and then keeps the entry forever
detail: frontend/sw.ts:163-167 stores the request's headers (including Authorization: Bearer <jwt>) at queue time and sw.ts:186 replays with those same headers. If the token was rotated or expired before the replay, the request 401s and the entry stays queued - a slow leak of dead requests and a confusing 'nothing syncs' symptom after a token change. Not an auth bypass (the stored token is the same one the app already had). Acceptance: either re-resolve the token at replay time (drop the stored Authorization header and let the replay path re-attach it) or drop and log entries that 401/403 with a bounded retry count; test with a stubbed token swap.
reasoning: Reported by the DF-HERMES-CANOPY-13 worker; foreman verified the queue/replay code paths at HEAD (sw.ts:158-190).
